stories.title: Investment Firm Garnett Station Partners Expands to 35K SF at 450 Park Avenue
stories.excerpt: Garnett Station Partners, a New York-based private equity investment firm and alternative asset manager, is expanding its office footprint in Midtown Manhattan, Commercial Observer has learned. Garnett has signed an 11.5-year lease to expand its footprint by 10,392 square feet on the entire seventh floor of SL Green Realty’s 450 Park Avenue, where it has been a tenant since 2023, according to a source with knowledge of the deal. The investment firm already occupies 24,963 square feet across the 33-story building’s entire 24th and 25th floors, as well as part of the 27th floor. The new expansion brings Garnett’s total footprint at 450 Park to 35,355 square feet. The asking rent for the new deal was $140 per square foot, according to the source. Newmark’s David Falk and Jason Greenstein brokered the deal for the tenadant, while CBRE and representatives from SL Green repped the landlord in-house. Spokespeople for SL Green and Garnett did not immediately respond to requests for comment, while Newmark declined to comment. Garnett, founded in 2013 by private equity veterans Matthew Perelman and Alex Sloane, relocated to 450 Park in 2023 from a previous office at 853 Broadway. The firm currently has approximately $4.5 billion in assets under management. Other tenants at 450 Park include private equity firm OceanSound, investment advisory services firm Steadfast Financial, and BankUnited, which just this month expanded to 27,392 square feet at the building. SL Green bought the office building on Park Avenue between East 56th and East 57th streets for $445 million in 2022. Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Garnett Station Partners expands 10,392 SF at SL Green's 450 Park Avenue, Midtown Manhattan.
11.5-year lease at $140/SF; total footprint grows to 35,355 SF across three floors.
Signals continued PE/alternative asset manager demand for Midtown trophy office space.
stories.summary: Garnett Station Partners, a NY-based PE firm, has expanded its footprint at SL Green Realty's 450 Park Avenue by 10,392 square feet on the seventh floor, bringing total occupancy to 35,355 square feet across multiple floors. The 11.5-year lease was struck at $140 per square foot. The deal represents strong tenant demand for premium Midtown Manhattan office despite broader market headwinds.
stories.impact: MINIMAL MULTIFAMILY IMPACT. This is a pure office transaction with no direct bearing on apartment supply, demand, or development feasibility. However, sustained PE and institutional tenant expansion in Midtown signals continued white-collar employment concentration in Manhattan, which underpins rental demand in adjacent residential submarkets (Murray Hill, Kips Bay, Turtle Bay), though the market is already well-supplied in those areas.

stories.title: Related Urban Secures $129M Financing for Downtown Miami Project
stories.excerpt: Related Urban Development Group said Thursday that it has arranged $129 million in financing for Gallery Lummus Parc, a 257-unit transit-oriented development in Downtown Miami. Greystone Real Estate Capital said it’s providing $80 million in construction financing and identified a $60 million permanent mortgage as a tax-exempt loan through Freddie Mac. Related Urban said additional financing sources include $27.1 million generated through the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit program; a $12.75 million State Apartment Incentive Loan from the Florida Housing Finance Corporation; a $5 million Documentary Surtax loan from Miami-Dade County; a $3 million American Rescue Plan Act loan from the City of Miami; and $6.4 million in Opportunity Zone investment from an entity affiliated with Related Group. Related Urban didn’t identify sources of the remaining $15 million in financing. The affordable housing project is on a 0.7-acre spot at 101 Northwest North River Drive and 395 Northwest First Street, next to Lummus Park and two blocks from Government Center Metrorail and Metromover station. Plans call for 27 stories of residential development and a five-level garage. Construction is set to begin this month and end in two years. The density is allowed because the site is in Miami-Dade County’s Rapid Transit Zone. More than 80 percent of Gallery Lummus Parc’s apartments will have rents tied to household income. That includes 167 units for tenants making between 20 percent and 80 percent of the area median income, along with 47 workforce units and 43 market-rate units. “We’re taking a compact county-owned site and creating homes for locals across a wide range of incomes,” Alberto Milo Jr., president of Related Urban, said in a statement. “It shows what’s possible when we pair housing with access to transit, jobs and essential services.” Jeff Ostrowski can be reached at jostrowski@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Related Urban secures $129M financing for Gallery Lummus Parc, 257-unit TOD in Downtown Miami.
Stack includes $80M construction (Greystone), $60M Freddie Mac permanent, $27.1M LIHTC, state/local subsidies.
Affordable-focused transit-oriented project on 0.7-acre site near Government Center signals density push and public subsidy availability.
stories.summary: Related Urban Development arranged $129 million in layered financing for Gallery Lummus Parc, a 257-unit transit-oriented affordable development in Downtown Miami at 101 NW North River Drive. The deal stacks $80M construction financing from Greystone, $60M Freddie Mac permanent tax-exempt loan, $27.1M LIHTC, $12.75M Florida Housing Finance Corp loan, $5M Miami-Dade surtax, $3M Miami ARP loan, and $6.4M Opportunity Zone capital. The project sits adjacent to Lummus Park and two blocks from Government Center.
stories.impact: CRITICAL MIAMI SIGNAL. Downtown Miami's TOD/infill corridor is receiving heavy public and institutional capital targeting affordable units—a strong indicator of both neighborhood trajectory and regulatory favorability for multifamily. The layered subsidy stack (LIHTC, state loan, county/city grants, OZ) shows government commitment to transit-oriented housing density. For developers: this validates pre-positioning for future Downtown Miami acquisitions and confirms the subsidy environment is functional, though project-level returns may be compressed by subsidy requirements.

stories.title: SoHo Office and Retail Property Refinanced Through ACORE Capital
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop, Inc. has arranged $216 million in bridge financing to refinance 568 Broadway, a mixed-use trophy asset located in Manhattan’s SoHo neighborhood. The Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory team served as exclusive advisor to a joint venture between Aurora Capital, Allied Partners and A&H Acquisitions. Aaron Appel, Dustin Stolly, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre arranged the financing with ACORE Capital. “Few assets can match this Broadway property’s combination of premier corner positioning, Broadway frontage, strong retail tenancy, recently upgraded infrastructure, and flexible office product,” said Stolly. “SoHo remains one of Manhattan’s most supply-constrained office and retail submarkets, with limited large-block inventory and minimal new competitive supply. That scarcity limits competitive leasing pressure while supporting future rent growth, occupancy durability, and long-term value.” 568 Broadway is a 12-story, 390,745-square-foot property comprising of office and retail space. The property’s approximately 70,870-square-foot retail component is 100% leased to Hugo Boss, Athletic Propulsion Labs, GU, and Equinox, while the office component is leased to a mix of tenants including Zocdoc, The Farmer’s Dog, and Milk Makeup. The post SoHo Office and Retail Property Refinanced Through ACORE Capital appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranges $216M bridge refinance for 568 Broadway, 12-story mixed-use SoHo property.
390,745 SF total: 70,870 SF retail (100% leased to Hugo Boss, APL, GU, Equinox); office portion not detailed.
Financing source ACORE Capital; broker emphasizes supply scarcity and minimal new competitive supply in SoHo office/retail.
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged $216 million in bridge financing from ACORE Capital to refinance 568 Broadway, a 12-story, 390,745-square-foot mixed-use property in Manhattan's SoHo. The retail component (70,870 SF) is fully leased to Hugo Boss, Athletic Propulsion Labs, GU, and Equinox. The deal's broker noted SoHo remains supply-constrained for office and retail with limited large-block inventory and minimal new competitive supply.
stories.impact: MINIMAL MULTIFAMILY RELEVANCE, but noteworthy for market signal: SoHo's tight office/retail supply and premium positioning are driving refinance capital flow and rent-growth narratives that support long-term asset durability. This reinforces SoHo's status as a stable, supply-constrained neighborhood—relevant context for any multifamily redevelopment activity in adjacent areas (NoLita, Lower East Side), though 568 Broadway itself is office/retail, not residential.

stories.title: Culver City Mixed-Use Secures $133M Bank OZK Loan
stories.excerpt: Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners have secured $132.7 million in construction financing from Bank OZK for ElevenOneEleven, a new mixed-use development in Culver City. Senior managing director Lou Friedel and managing director Keith Rosso of Berkadia Los Angeles arranged the financing on behalf of Lincoln and McCourt. Located at 11111 Jefferson Blvd., ElevenOneEleven will tnclude 344 residences, including 52 affordable units, along with 2,000 square feet of retail and 17,520 square feet of publicly accessible outdoor space. “This financing marks a critical milestone for ElevenOneEleven, providing the capital needed to move into the next phase of bringing our vision for this project to life,” said Stephen Lindgren, SVP and Los Angeles market lead at Lincoln. “McCourt has been an exceptional development partner throughout the process, and our collaboration reflects a shared conviction in the project and what it will bring to the Culver City community.” The post Culver City Mixed-Use Secures $133M Bank OZK Loan appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Lincoln Property/McCourt Partners secure $132.7M construction financing from Bank OZK for Culver City project.
ElevenOneEleven: 344 residences (52 affordable), 2,000 SF retail, 17,520 SF outdoor space at 11111 Jefferson Blvd.
Marks critical financing milestone; demonstrates LA bank appetite for mixed-use infill with affordable component.
stories.summary: Lincoln Property Company and McCourt Partners closed $132.7 million in construction financing from Bank OZK for ElevenOneEleven, a mixed-use development in Culver City at 11111 Jefferson Blvd. The project includes 344 residences (52 affordable units), 2,000 square feet of retail, and 17,520 square feet of publicly accessible outdoor space. Berkadia Los Angeles brokered the financing.
stories.impact: CULVER CITY DEVELOPMENT MOMENTUM. Bank OZK's $133M commitment signals ongoing construction financing availability for mid-size LA infill multifamily with mixed-use and affordable components. Culver City's continued density and infrastructure investment make it an attractive secondary market for future development. The 15% affordable unit requirement and robust outdoor space suggest Culver City's regulatory environment supports higher-density, amenity-rich projects—relevant for gauging entitlement and feasibility timelines in LA's Westside submarket.

stories.title: Union Investment Sells Meatpacking District Retail Condo for $27M
stories.excerpt: A high-profile retail space in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District has traded. Union Investment Real Estate, a Germany-based real estate investment manager, sold a retail condo unit at the base of the mixed-use 415 West 13th Street for $26.5 million, according to city records made public Wednesday. The buyer of Unit 1N was the LLC West Gotham Re Projects Corporation, with Nicolo Forni as a signatory. Further details about the buyer and Forni were unclear, as the address tied to the LLC was a law firm. Union Investment bought the condo for $18 million in 2012, records show. Karim Josef Esch, head of real estate management at Union Investment, and Adam Iranyi, head of investment management at Union, signed the new deal for the seller. It’s unclear what tenant, if any, currently occupies the roughly 15,000-square-foot Unit 1N at the building between Ninth Avenue and Washington Street. Current retail tenants at the property include hair salon Bumble and Bumble, art gallery Affirmation Arts and fitness club WndrHLTH Club. Office tenants in the upper floors include Estee Lauder and aviation supplier FTAI. AllSaints signed a lease for 3,775 square feet there in 2023, but seems to have since closed. A spokesperson for Union Investment declined to comment on the buyer’s identity. A spokesperson for Ripco Real Estate, which has worked on past deals at the building, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. In July 2025, MacArthur Holdings, which owns roughly 68 percent of the building, landed a $47 million loan to refinance its respective retail and office condos at the property, as Commercial Observer previously reported. MacArthur owns units 1S and 3S, which span a total of 62,707 square feet. Isabelle Durso can be reached at idurso@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Union Investment sells Meatpacking District retail condo (415 West 13th Street, Unit 1N) for $26.5M.
15,000 SF unit; buyer LLC West Gotham Re Projects; 2012 purchase price $18 million (47% appreciation over 12 years).
Current building tenants include Bumble and Bumble, WndrHLTH Club, Estee Lauder; signals retail/mixed-use portfolio activity.
stories.summary: Union Investment Real Estate sold a retail condo unit (Unit 1N, ~15,000 SF) at 415 West 13th Street in Manhattan's Meatpacking District for $26.5 million. Union had purchased the unit in 2012 for $18 million, representing approximately 47% appreciation. The buyer was identified as LLC West Gotham Re Projects Corporation. The building houses retail tenants (Bumble and Bumble, WndrHLTH Club, Affirmation Arts) and office tenants (Estee Lauder, FTAI).
stories.impact: MINIMAL MULTIFAMILY IMPACT. This is a retail condo disposition in a high-profile mixed-use building; no residential supply or demand signal. However, the Meatpacking District's continued retail and creative tenant stability (hair, fitness, art, luxury goods, aviation) underscores the neighborhood's mixed-use vitality and suggests any nearby multifamily remains well-positioned for young professional/creative class renters, though this is context-reinforcing rather than market-shifting.

stories.title: BridgeCity Lends $84M on Midtown East Office-to-Resi Conversion
stories.excerpt: CSC Real Estate has landed $83.5 million of acquisition and construction financing to reposition a Midtown East office property into luxury apartments, Commercial Observer has learned. BridgeCity Capital provided the loan for CSC’s planned 136-unit project at 136 East 57th Street in a deal that closed Oct. 13. CSC acquired the 20-story building for $10 million from Cerco Funding in March, PincusCo. reported at the time. The 92,582-square-foot 136 East 57th Street property, at the corner of East 57th Street and Lexington Avenue, was built in 1931 and renovated in 1987. It’s across the street from another office-to-resi conversion at 135 East 57th Street, known as Tower 57, that TF Cornerstone is executing. “BridgeCity is excited about this transaction, given the property’s exceptional location and the strength of the underlying business plan,” EJ Ehrlich, director of originations for BridgeCity, said in a statement. “We believe this project represents a compelling opportunity to reposition a well-located Manhattan asset into a premier luxury residential property.” CSC Real Estate did not immediately return a request for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: BridgeCity Capital closes $83.5M acquisition/construction financing for CSC Real Estate's office-to-resi conversion.
136 East 57th Street, Midtown East: 20-story, 92,582 SF, 136-unit luxury apartment project; CSC acquired for $10M in March.
Conversion trend continues; property benefits from corner Lexington Avenue location; TF Cornerstone executing similar project across street (Tower 57).
stories.summary: CSC Real Estate secured $83.5 million in acquisition and construction financing from BridgeCity Capital to convert 136 East 57th Street in Midtown East into 136 luxury apartments. The 20-story, 92,582-square-foot office building was acquired by CSC for $10 million in March 2026. The project closed October 13. The property is located at the corner of East 57th Street and Lexington Avenue, directly across from Tower 57, a similar office-to-resi conversion by TF Cornerstone.
stories.impact: MIDTOWN EAST CONVERSION ACCELERATION. BridgeCity's willingness to lend $84M on a $10M acquisition signals strong conviction in Manhattan office-to-resi arbitrage and lender confidence in market absorption. The clustering of conversions (Tower 57 across the street) indicates coordinated landlord/developer repositioning in response to structural office demand decline. For Trammell Crow: this validates Midtown East as an active conversion corridor and signals potential acquisition opportunities in older office stock at attractive basis, though lenders are now pricing in execution risk and lengthy lease-up timelines, widening hurdle rates.

stories.title: News Outlet Semafor Takes 12K SF at 495 Broadway
stories.excerpt: The news never sleeps, and journalists want a comfy space to do their critical work. Digital news organization Semafor has inked a 12,000-square-foot lease at WB Property Group’s 495 Broadway just off Broome Street in SoHo, tenant broker Okada & Company confirmed to Commercial Observer. The lease was first reported by Traded. The deal represents a relocation for Semafor, which will relocate about four blocks north from 394 Broadway. “We are so thrilled to have represented Semafor in their office space expansion in SoHo,” Okada’s Christopher Okada, who represented Semafor alongside Ken Lerner, told CO. “It’s an incredible building with a wonderful landlord group that’s been in the area for many, many decades.” The length of the deal was not disclosed. The asking rent was $100 per square foot for the SoHo office space. JLL’s Dana Goldman and Brett Harvey represented the landlord in the deal. Spokespeople for Semafor and JLL did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Completed in 1893, 495 Broadway is an eight-story, Art Nouveau building with 12- to 15-foot vaulted ceilings, exposed brick, hardwood floors and outdoor space on the rooftop. Other tenants at 495 Broadway include wellness retreat Lumora Spa, multi-label fashion showroom and wholesaler The News, and apparel retailer Proenza Schouler. Amanda Schiavo can be reached at aschiavo@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Semafor (digital news org) leases 12,000 SF at WB Property Group's 495 Broadway in SoHo.
Asking rent $100/SF; relocation from 394 Broadway (four blocks south); lease term not disclosed.
Signals continued media/creative tenant demand in SoHo core; JLL represented landlord.
stories.summary: Digital news organization Semafor inked a 12,000-square-foot lease at 495 Broadway in SoHo (just off Broome Street), relocating from 394 Broadway four blocks south. The asking rent was $100 per square foot. The 1893 Art Nouveau building is owned by WB Property Group. JLL represented the landlord; Okada & Company represented Semafor.
stories.impact: MINIMAL MULTIFAMILY IMPACT. This is an office lease renewal/migration within SoHo's core media/creative cluster. The $100/SF asking rent reaffirms SoHo's premium office positioning but signals no supply, demand, or financing shift for apartment development. Contextually, media tenant demand in SoHo reflects the neighborhood's appeal to knowledge workers and creatives, which supports demand for nearby residential, but this lease alone does not shift multifamily market conditions.

stories.title: The Ride, Like Most Business, Was About Navigating the Journey
stories.excerpt: By Mark Strauss Editor’s note: This past April, managing director, capital markets Mark Strauss of Walker & Dunlop set out on a triple mission: to raise $1 million for No Kid Hungry, to raise awareness of childhood hunger, and to complete a coast-to-coast bicycle ride. Here, he recounts his experiences along his journey from Corona del Mar to Rehoboth Beach, DE. On April 17, my 73rd birthday, I clipped into my pedals at Lookout Point in Corona del Mar with the Pacific Ocean behind me and Rehoboth Beach, DE, more than 3,000 miles ahead. The objective sounded simple enough: ride across America and raise $1 million for No Kid Hungry. Of course, most goals sound simpler when reduced to one sentence.  I had trained for months. We had mapped the route, identified hotels, planned rest days, assembled equipment and created contingencies. Karen, my wife, and Scott, our driver, my body and part-time bike mechanic, followed in a 31-foot Thor Outlaw RV that would become mobile office, locker room, kitchen, bike shop, media center and mission control. I thought we had a plan.  We did. What I had not fully appreciated was how often the plan would have to change.  Over the next sixty-nine days, I rode roughly 3,200 miles through thirteen states. There were mountains, deserts, headwinds, hail, road closures, mechanical problems, wrong turns, a back problem  and more peanut butter than I care to remember. There were also extraordinary people, remarkable landscapes, an education in how the country actually works and a lot of time to think.  When I came home, I began writing down observations from the road. Many had nothing to do with cycling. stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop's Mark Strauss undertook a 3,200-mile cross-country bicycle ride from Corona del Mar, California to Rehoboth Beach, Delaware over 69 days to raise $1 million for No Kid Hungry charity. The article is a first-person narrative of planning, execution, and adaptation during the journey.

stories.title: Consumer Goods Companies Scrutinize CRE Portfolios As Technology Spending Lags
stories.excerpt: Consumer goods companies are focusing on supply chain disruptions and shifts in consumer spending habits to better manage their real estate portfolios, according to a JLL report. The company’s findings are based on 48 responses from consumer goods industry leaders. Close to 48% of respondents said their organizations The firm’s latest corporate real estate pulse survey included 48 responses from consumer goods industry leaders. Nearly 48% of respondents said their organizations are examining supply chains, “a notable 10 percentage points above the all-industry rate of 37.9% and the sharpest gap among priorities tracked in the survey,” according to JLL. While the data is essential for decision-making, JLL said that technology investment has yet to catch up, with 16.7% of consumer goods respondents anticipating growth in their CRE technology budgets over the next three years, compared to 30.6% across all industries. Also being examined is the workforce, as 39.6% of respondents said they’ve downsized their labor, compared to 31.6% across industries. Additionally, 37.5% said they expect office use rates to increase over the next 12 months. At the same time, 31.3% of respondents expect their CRE budgets to increase, compared to 24% across industries. “Where those dollars go matters: upgrades for higher production, space for more employees, or better utilization data that reveals opportunities to consolidate or redirect investment,” according to JLL. JLL recommended building a reliable data foundation, using technology to increase capacity and implementing a flexible portfolio strategy. “A shopper can put one product back on the shelf,” the report said. “A consumer goods company has to decide what happens to the factory, warehouse, office or brand behind it. That decision starts with knowing what you have.” The post Consumer Goods Companies Scrutinize CRE Portfolios As Technology Spending Lags appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL survey of 48 consumer goods industry leaders: 48% examining supply chain, 39.6% downsized labor.
Only 16.7% expect CRE tech budget growth (vs. 30.6% all industries); 37.5% expect office use rate increase.
Indicates consumer goods sector rightsizing real estate portfolios amid supply chain pressures and cost consciousness.
stories.summary: A JLL corporate real estate pulse survey of 48 consumer goods industry leaders found that nearly 48% are examining supply chains (10 points above all-industry average), 39.6% have downsized labor, and only 16.7% anticipate CRE technology budget growth over three years (vs. 30.6% across all industries). Additionally, 37.5% expect office use rates to increase over the next 12 months, and 31.3% expect overall CRE budgets to rise.
stories.impact: INDIRECT MARKET SIGNAL: Consumer goods companies represent significant suburban logistics/distribution real estate demand and some urban office footprints. Labor downsizing (39.6% vs. 31.6% all-industry) and technology underinvestment signal cost-cutting and potential real estate footprint rationalization. However, 37.5% expecting office use rate increases is counter-intuitive and may indicate selective hub consolidation rather than expansion—relevant for understanding which markets (dense urban centers) will attract consumer goods HQs, influencing white-collar employment and residential demand in those metros. Not a direct multifamily signal, but contextual for workforce demand modeling.
